content.explanation: Programs need memory to store data. In C++, developers often allocate and free memory manually. Mistakes can create leaks, crashes, and security problems. JavaScript simplifies this process through garbage collection. The engine automatically identifies unused objects and reclaims their memory. While this reduces complexity, memory leaks can still occur if references are kept unnecessarily.
content.example: When an object is no longer referenced, the JavaScript engine can remove it from memory.
content.analogy: A cleaning service removes unused items automatically.

mcqs.question: An object becomes unreachable. What may happen?
A developer keeps unnecessary references. Result?
Garbage collection eliminates all memory leaks.
